newsitem.title: CANADA: Bank Montreal says C$2.5 bln not earmarked.
newsitem.headline: Bank Montreal says C$2.5 bln not earmarked.

text.p: Bank of Montreal said on Tuesday that it had not earmarked a C$2.5 billion shelf offering program that it announced today.
Bank of Montreal spokesman Paul Gammal told Reuters that the money raised from the program would be used to finance existing debt and support growth.
"It's going to be used to re-finance existing subordinated debt as it comes due and to support growth," Gammal said. "So it's not earmarked for anything in particular."
He said that although the offering would last for two years, the bank may not issue the entire amount.
Bank of Montreal announced the establishment of a C$2.5 billion North American shelf offering program to issue subordinated debt securities to investors in Canada and the United States.

Bank of Montreal said that combined with its European medium-term note program, the North American shelf would provide the bank with the ability to respond to attractive financing opportunities in debt markets around the world.

The bank's North American Shelf will include two medium- term note programs, one in Canada and the other in the United States. The Canadian program will provide access to investors in Canada and is being established by way of a debt shelf prospectus and prospectus supplement filed with various provincial securities commissions.
